drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 77-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.6, creatinine 0.97, hemoglobin 12.9, platelets 278, sodium 141, wbc 8.9; vitals dbp 67-70, heart_rate 85-89, map 90-92, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 133-138, spo2 96-98, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 0.99, hemoglobin 12.8, platelets 275, sodium 141, wbc 8.7; vitals dbp 67-71, heart_rate 85-89, map 90-93, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 134-139, spo2 96-98, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 77-year-old female, length of stay 3 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
